words.enDefinition: an organisation that puts on stage plays or other theatrical productions

examples.en: The student theatre company chose three short plays for the spring semester.
examples.zh: 学生「剧团」为春季学期选了三部短剧。

examples.en: My classmate joined a theatre company that performs new plays by local writers.
examples.zh: 同学加入了一个「剧团」，演出本地作者创作的新剧。

words.enDefinition: theatre made by and for people living in a local community

examples.en: I met some local actors through community theatre during my first summer here.
examples.zh: 来这里的第一个夏天，我通过「社区戏剧」认识了一些本地演员。

examples.en: Our campus group collaborated with community theatre volunteers on a short performance.
examples.zh: 我们学校的社团和「社区戏剧」的志愿者合作演了一出短剧。

words.enDefinition: theatre outside the mainstream, often small-scale, experimental, or independently produced

examples.en: We saw some fringe theatre in a tiny room above a café.
examples.zh: 我们在一家咖啡馆楼上的小房间里看了场「非主流戏剧」。

examples.en: The drama department brought in two fringe theatre directors to discuss their work.
examples.zh: 戏剧系请来两位「非主流戏剧」导演分享他们的作品。

words.enDefinition: the staged presentation of a play or other theatrical work

examples.en: The students chose a small theatre production they could tour to neighbouring campuses.
examples.zh: 同学们选了个小型「剧场演出」，可以到附近的校园巡演。

examples.en: I worked on my first theatre production in the spring of my final year.
examples.zh: 大四春季，我第一次参与了「剧场演出」。

words.enDefinition: a version of an existing story created to be performed onstage

examples.en: Our class watched a stage adaptation of a novel we had just finished.
examples.zh: 我们班看了一部「舞台改编作品」，原著是刚读完的一本小说。

examples.en: The stage adaptation used just two actors to tell the entire story.
examples.zh: 这部「舞台改编作品」只用两位演员就讲完了整个故事。

words.enDefinition: a piece of drama written to be performed by actors onstage

examples.en: The students wrote a stage play about strangers waiting for the same bus.
examples.zh: 同学们写了一部「舞台剧」，讲几个陌生人等同一班公交的故事。

examples.en: I had only seen the film before watching the stage play on campus.
examples.zh: 我以前只看过电影，后来才在学校看到这部「舞台剧」。

words.enDefinition: a play that consists of just one main dramatic section

examples.en: My classmate wrote a one-act play set in the university's laundry room.
examples.zh: 同学写了部「独幕剧」，故事发生在学校的洗衣房。

examples.en: We stayed for a one-act play after the longer production had finished.
examples.zh: 那部长剧结束后，我们留下又看了部「独幕剧」。

words.enDefinition: a form of stage performance that combines acting, songs, and movement

examples.en: I joined a musical theatre workshop to practise singing while moving onstage.
examples.zh: 我参加了一个「音乐剧表演」工作坊，练习在台上边走动边唱歌。

examples.en: The university's musical theatre society held an informal performance in the library courtyard.
examples.zh: 学校的「音乐剧表演」社在图书馆的庭院办了一场非正式演出。

words.enDefinition: a simple performance space with flexible arrangements for staging and seating

examples.en: The audience sat very close to the actors in the black box theatre.
examples.zh: 在「黑匣子剧场」里，观众坐得离演员很近。

examples.en: We chose the black box theatre because we wanted to change the seating layout.
examples.zh: 我们选了「黑匣子剧场」，因为想改动座位布局。

collocations: perform in a black box theatre

words.enDefinition: a theatre arrangement where the audience sits around the central stage

examples.en: The school staged the play as theatre in the round, with the audience on all sides.
examples.zh: 学校采用了「环绕式剧场」，观众从各个方向围着表演者坐。

examples.en: I had never seen theatre in the round before our class visited that small venue.
examples.zh: 在全班去那家小场馆前，我从没见过「环绕式剧场」。

collocations: staging for theatre in the round
space designed for theatre in the round

words.enDefinition: the arch or frame separating a conventional stage from its audience

examples.en: My seat gave me a clear view of the painted proscenium arch.
examples.zh: 从我的座位能清楚看到彩绘的「镜框式台口」。

examples.en: The proscenium arch made the stage look like a giant picture frame.
examples.zh: 「镜框式台口」让舞台看起来像一个巨大的画框。

words.enDefinition: a stage extending into the audience with seating on three sides

examples.en: The actors sometimes faced away from us on the thrust stage.
examples.zh: 在「伸入观众席的舞台」上表演时，演员有时会背向我们。

examples.en: We learned how to perform on a thrust stage during the workshop.
examples.zh: 工作坊上，我们学习了如何在「伸入观众席的舞台」上表演。

words.enDefinition: areas at the sides of a stage hidden from audiences

examples.en: We waited in the wings until the stage manager nodded at us.
examples.zh: 我们在「侧幕区」等着，直到舞台监督朝我们点头。

examples.en: I watched from the wings while my classmates finished the first scene.
examples.zh: 同学演完第一场时，我在「侧幕区」观看。

words.enDefinition: at or towards the back of the stage, away from the audience

examples.en: The actor moved upstage so everyone could see the other two performers.
examples.zh: 演员往「舞台后部」移动，让观众能看到另外两位表演者。

examples.en: I had to stand upstage when my partner made her entrance.
examples.zh: 搭档登场的时候，我得站在「舞台后部」。

words.enDefinition: at or towards the front of the stage, near the audience

examples.en: I stepped downstage so the audience could actually see my face.
examples.zh: 我往「舞台前部」迈了几步，好让观众看清我的脸。

examples.en: The dancer waited downstage while the final piece of music started.
examples.zh: 最后一段音乐开始时，那位舞者等在「舞台前部」。

words.enDefinition: an area below or in front of the stage where musicians play

examples.en: We could hear musicians tuning their instruments in the orchestra pit before the show.
examples.zh: 开演前，我们听到乐手在「乐池」里给乐器调音。

examples.en: The orchestra pit was small, so only four musicians played that evening.
examples.zh: 当晚的「乐池」不大，只有四位乐手演奏。

words.enDefinition: a room where performers can wait or relax before going onstage

examples.en: We waited in the green room until the first performance had ended.
examples.zh: 我们在「演员休息室」等到第一场表演结束。

examples.en: My friend left a bottle of water for me in the green room.
examples.zh: 朋友在「演员休息室」给我留了一瓶水。

words.enDefinition: a room where performers change clothes and prepare their appearance

examples.en: Three student dancers shared a dressing room behind the small stage that night.
examples.zh: 那晚，三位学生舞者共用小舞台后的一间「演出更衣室」。

examples.en: I left my shoes in the dressing room after the final performance.
examples.zh: 最后一场演出结束后，我把鞋落在了「演出更衣室」。

words.enDefinition: the person who coordinates rehearsals and keeps a live performance running

examples.en: The stage manager reminded us when we needed to be ready to enter.
examples.zh: 「舞台监督」提醒我们什么时候该为上场做好准备。

examples.en: I watched the stage manager make notes during our first full run.
examples.zh: 第一次完整走排时，我看着「舞台监督」记下了要点。

words.enDefinition: a person who helps the director organise rehearsals and develop the show

examples.en: Our assistant director asked us to repeat the scene at a slower pace.
examples.zh: 我们的「助理导演」请我们用慢一点的节奏再演一遍这场戏。

examples.en: The assistant director took notes while the director talked to the actors.
examples.zh: 导演和演员说话时，「助理导演」在一旁记笔记。

words.enDefinition: someone who writes plays for the stage or performance

examples.en: A local playwright answered our questions after the staged reading in class.
examples.zh: 课上做完剧本朗读，一位本地「剧作家」回答了我们的问题。

examples.en: The playwright changed the ending after hearing students read it aloud.
examples.zh: 听学生把剧本读出声后，「剧作家」改了结尾。

words.enDefinition: someone who supports a production through research and analysis of the script

examples.en: Our dramaturg researched how students spoke during the period of the play.
examples.zh: 我们的「戏剧构作顾问」研究了该剧时代的学生是怎么说话的。

examples.en: The dramaturg wrote a short note explaining the setting for the audience.
examples.zh: 「戏剧构作顾问」写了一段简短说明，给观众介绍剧中的场景背景。

words.enDefinition: someone who creates and organises movement for a dance or performance

examples.en: The choreographer gave the two dancers different steps for the final section.
examples.zh: 「编舞」给两位舞者在最后一段安排了不同的舞步。

examples.en: Our choreographer asked us to practise the movement without music first.
examples.zh: 我们的「编舞」让我们先不放音乐练一练动作。

words.enDefinition: the person in charge of the music in a production

examples.en: The music director listened to the singers before setting the rehearsal schedule.
examples.zh: 「音乐总监」先听过歌手的演唱，再定排练日程。

examples.en: Our music director helped the cast match its singing to the piano.
examples.zh: 我们的「音乐总监」帮演员们把歌声和钢琴配合起来。

words.enDefinition: a list showing who has been chosen to perform each role

examples.en: We refreshed the page until the cast list appeared after our auditions.
examples.zh: 试镜结束后，我们不断刷新页面，直到「演员名单」公布。

examples.en: The cast list included students from the music department and the drama club.
examples.zh: 「演员名单」里既有音乐系的学生，也有戏剧社的成员。

words.enDefinition: a performer who learns a role to cover when needed

examples.en: The understudy went on after one of the actors lost their voice.
examples.zh: 有位演员嗓子哑了，「替补演员」上场演了这个角色。

examples.en: I worked as an understudy and practised the same lines every week.
examples.zh: 我当「替补演员」，每周都练同样的台词。

words.enDefinition: a performer kept available to replace a principal actor when needed

examples.en: The standby performer waited backstage in case the lead singer could not continue.
examples.zh: 「随时待命的替补演员」在后台等着，以防主唱不能继续演出。

examples.en: One standby performer learned the lead role without taking a regular ensemble part.
examples.zh: 有一位「随时待命的替补演员」排练了主角的戏份，平时在这出戏里没有固定角色。

words.enDefinition: a group of performers working together as a coordinated unit

examples.en: Our class formed an acting ensemble for a series of short student plays.
examples.zh: 我们班为一系列学生短剧组建了一个「表演团体」。

examples.en: The acting ensemble built the whole scene around one actor's quiet entrance.
examples.zh: 「表演团体」把整场戏围绕一位演员悄悄上场来编排。

words.enDefinition: a performer prepared to cover several ensemble parts as needed

examples.en: The swing performer had learned three of the dancers' parts by opening night.
examples.zh: 到首演之夜，「多角色替补演员」已经学会了三位舞者的戏份。

examples.en: A swing performer took over one ensemble part when a dancer was absent.
examples.zh: 一位舞者缺席时，「多角色替补演员」顶上了一个群舞角色。

words.enDefinition: an announcement asking performers to audition for roles in a production

examples.en: I saw a casting call for the student musical outside the rehearsal room.
examples.zh: 我在排练室外看到那部学生音乐剧的「演员招募通告」。

examples.en: The casting call asked for people who had never acted onstage before.
examples.zh: 「演员招募通告」面向以前没上台演过戏的人。

words.enDefinition: an invitation to audition again after an initial tryout

examples.en: The audition callback arrived while I was waiting for the bus after class.
examples.zh: 我下课后等公交时，收到了「复试通知」。

examples.en: My roommate took the audition callback as a sign they liked her reading.
examples.zh: 室友收到「复试通知」，觉得他们大概喜欢她试镜时的朗读。

words.enDefinition: a reading from a script without time to practise first

examples.en: I did a cold read from a scene they handed me at the door.
examples.zh: 他们在门口递给我一场戏的剧本，我当场做了一次「无准备试读」。

examples.en: For my cold read, they gave me part of an unfamiliar student play.
examples.zh: 「无准备试读」时，他们给了我一段从没读过的学生剧本。

words.enDefinition: short sections of a script used by performers at an audition

examples.en: The audition sides for both main roles were on the theatre website.
examples.zh: 两个主要角色的「试镜用剧本选段」都在剧团网站上。

examples.en: My friend printed the audition sides before going to the rehearsal room.
examples.zh: 朋友去排练室之前，打印了「试镜用剧本选段」。

words.enDefinition: a session where performers read a play aloud from start to finish

examples.en: We had our first read-through around a long table in the library.
examples.zh: 我们围坐在图书馆的一张长桌旁，进行了第一次「剧本通读」。

examples.en: The writer attended the read-through and listened without interrupting the actors.
examples.zh: 作者参加了「剧本通读」，演员朗读时一直听着，没有打断。

words.enDefinition: a public presentation of a script with limited staging and movement

examples.en: The club held a staged reading before deciding whether to produce the play.
examples.zh: 社团先办了一场「剧本朗读演出」，再决定要不要正式演出。

examples.en: At the staged reading, the performers used chairs and did not wear costumes.
examples.zh: 「剧本朗读演出」时，表演者用了椅子，没有穿戏服。

collocations: staged reading of a new play

words.enDefinition: the time when performers or crew are expected to arrive

examples.en: Our call time was before lunch, so we brought snacks with us.
examples.zh: 「规定到场时间」在午饭前，所以我们带了些零食。

examples.en: I asked the stage manager whether the call time had been changed.
examples.zh: 我问舞台监督，「规定到场时间」有没有改。

words.enDefinition: a notice saying who is needed at a rehearsal and when

examples.en: The rehearsal call asked only the dancers to come in on Monday.
examples.zh: 「排练到场通知」只要求舞者周一过来。

examples.en: I checked the rehearsal call to see when our scene would be rehearsed.
examples.zh: 我看了看「排练到场通知」，确认我们那场戏什么时候排。

words.enDefinition: the planned positions and movements of performers during a scene

examples.en: We changed the blocking so that both actors could be seen.
examples.zh: 我们调整了「舞台走位」，让观众能看见两位演员。

examples.en: The director added new blocking for the scene with the long table.
examples.zh: 导演为有长桌的那场戏加了新的「舞台走位」。

words.enDefinition: an instruction in a script about action, movement, or staging

examples.en: The stage direction said to pause before the next actor entered the room.
examples.zh: 「舞台指示」要求在下一位演员进屋前停顿一下。

examples.en: I marked a stage direction in my script so I wouldn't miss it.
examples.zh: 我在剧本上标出一处「舞台指示」，免得漏掉。

words.enDefinition: to reach the exact position specified for you onstage

examples.en: You have to hit your mark before the lights change in this scene.
examples.zh: 在这场戏的灯光变换前，你得「走到规定站位」。

examples.en: It's easier to hit your mark if you remember where your partner stands.
examples.zh: 记住搭档站在哪儿，就更容易「走到规定站位」。

collocations: practise how to hit your mark

words.enDefinition: to repeat the words you need to say in a performance

examples.en: You can practise your lines in the green room while the crew sets up.
examples.zh: 工作人员布置时，你可以在演员休息室「练习台词」。

examples.en: It's easier to practise your lines with someone who knows the scene already.
examples.zh: 和已经熟悉这场戏的人一起「练习台词」会比较容易。

collocations: practise your lines with a friend

words.enDefinition: able to perform from memory without reading the script

examples.en: I was finally off book by the time we moved into the theatre.
examples.zh: 我们搬进剧场排练时，我终于能「脱稿」了。

examples.en: The actors were off book, but there were still a few missed lines.
examples.zh: 演员已经能「脱稿」了，不过还有几处漏词。

words.enDefinition: the way an actor says a particular line of a script

examples.en: The director liked my second line reading because it sounded less formal.
examples.zh: 导演更喜欢我第二次的「台词说法」，因为听起来没那么正式。

examples.en: We tried a slower line reading for that short question in the play.
examples.zh: 剧中那个简短问题，我们试了试更慢的「台词说法」。

words.enDefinition: to ask for the next words after forgetting part of a script

examples.en: We could call for a line if we got stuck during the first rehearsal.
examples.zh: 第一次排练卡住时，我们可以「忘词时请人提示」。

examples.en: I heard my scene partner call for a line and waited before moving across the stage.
examples.zh: 我听见搭档「忘词请人提示」，就等了一下再走到舞台另一边。

collocations: need to call for a line
remember to call for a line
hear someone call for a line

words.enDefinition: to make up a spoken line without following the script

examples.en: The theatre game asked each of us to improvise a line about the room.
examples.zh: 戏剧游戏让我们每个人针对这个房间「即兴说一句台词」。

examples.en: She wanted to improvise a line after the director cut the original joke.
examples.zh: 导演删掉原来的笑话后，她想「即兴说一句台词」。

words.enDefinition: the act of coming onto the stage during a performance

examples.en: The actor's stage entrance was meant to happen while the lights were still low.
examples.zh: 原定这位演员要在灯光还很暗时「登场」。

examples.en: I marked my stage entrance in the margin next to my first line.
examples.zh: 我在第一句台词旁边的空白处标出了自己的「登场」时机。

words.enDefinition: the act of leaving the stage during a performance

examples.en: The performer timed her stage exit with the last beat of the music.
examples.zh: 那位表演者掐准音乐最后一拍「退场」。

examples.en: Our director moved one chair so the stage exit looked more natural.
examples.zh: 导演挪了一把椅子，让「退场」看起来更自然。

words.enDefinition: tells performers to get into position for a performance or scene

examples.en: The stage manager said "Take your places," and we went quietly to our spots.
examples.zh: 舞台监督说「各就各位」，我们就轻轻走到各自的位置。

examples.en: Take your places behind the curtain before the music for the next scene starts.
examples.zh: 下一场的音乐放起来之前，请在幕布后「各就各位」。

collocations: wait for the signal to take your places

words.enDefinition: a signal for a planned change in stage lighting

examples.en: A lighting cue brought the lights down as the last actor left.
examples.zh: 最后一名演员退场时，灯光按照「灯光提示」暗了下来。

examples.en: We repeated the ending to practise the final lighting cue once more.
examples.zh: 我们重排了结尾，再练一次最后的「灯光提示」。

words.enDefinition: a signal for music or an effect to begin or change

examples.en: The stage manager called the sound cue for the doorbell during rehearsal.
examples.zh: 排练时，舞台监督发出「音效提示」，让门铃声响起。

examples.en: We repeated the sound cue because the rain effect started too early.
examples.zh: 模拟下雨的声音放早了，我们又过了一遍「音效提示」。

words.enDefinition: to fail to respond at the right moment to a signal

examples.en: It's easy to miss a cue when several people are talking at once.
examples.zh: 好几个人同时说话时，很容易「错过表演提示」。

examples.en: I didn't want to miss a cue in our first scene together.
examples.zh: 第一次合作演这场戏，我可不想「错过表演提示」。

collocations: try not to miss a cue

words.enDefinition: a rehearsal that integrates equipment cues with the performers' actions

examples.en: Our technical rehearsal took longer because we paused to check each lighting change.
examples.zh: 每次灯光变化我们都停下来核对，所以「技术合成排练」时间长了一些。

examples.en: At the technical rehearsal, I heard the scene's new music for the first time.
examples.zh: 「技术合成排练」时，我第一次听到那场戏的新配乐。

words.enDefinition: a technical rehearsal moving between cues while skipping intervening sections

examples.en: We did a cue-to-cue instead of performing all the scenes that morning.
examples.zh: 那天上午，我们做了「逐个提示点合成排练」，没有把每场戏都演一遍。

examples.en: The cue-to-cue let the crew check two quick changes in lighting.
examples.zh: 「逐个提示点合成排练」让工作人员检查了两次快速的灯光变换。

words.enDefinition: a rehearsal in which performers go through a piece or a substantial section from start to finish

examples.en: We finished the first run-through just before the rehearsal room closed.
examples.zh: 排练室快关门时，我们刚完成第一次「完整走排」。

examples.en: The director watched the run-through without stopping to give notes.
examples.zh: 导演看完了「完整走排」，没有叫停来提意见。

words.enDefinition: to offer feedback on what performers should change after a rehearsal

examples.en: The director waited until the end of the rehearsal to give notes.
examples.zh: 导演等到排练结束才「给演员提调整意见」。

examples.en: My choreography tutor likes to give notes after watching the whole piece.
examples.zh: 我的编舞老师喜欢看完整段表演再「给演员提调整意见」。

words.enDefinition: a room set aside for practising a performance

examples.en: We put tape on the rehearsal room floor to mark our positions.
examples.zh: 我们用胶带在「排练室」地上标出站位。

examples.en: My classmates waited outside the rehearsal room until the dancers had finished.
examples.zh: 同学们在「排练室」外等到舞者练完。

words.enDefinition: a session to check that a performer's outfit fits properly

examples.en: My costume fitting was right after class, so I brought my dance shoes.
examples.zh: 「戏服试穿」就在课后，我带来了舞鞋。

examples.en: The costume designer took notes during my costume fitting on Tuesday.
examples.zh: 周二我「试穿戏服」时，服装设计师在一旁记了笔记。

words.enDefinition: a costume change that a performer makes very rapidly during a show

examples.en: I had less than a minute for a quick change between scenes.
examples.zh: 两场戏之间，我要在不到一分钟内「快速换装」。

examples.en: One wardrobe volunteer helped me with a quick change in the wings.
examples.zh: 一位服装组志愿者在侧幕后帮我「快速换装」。

words.enDefinition: an object used by a performer during a stage production

examples.en: The umbrella was a stage prop from an earlier student production.
examples.zh: 那把伞是之前一部学生剧用过的「舞台道具」。

examples.en: I borrowed a stage prop that looked exactly like my old suitcase.
examples.zh: 我借了一件和我的旧行李箱一模一样的「舞台道具」。

words.enDefinition: a table near the stage where props are laid out

examples.en: I left the fake letter on the prop table behind the curtain.
examples.zh: 我把那封假信留在了幕布后面的「道具摆放台」上。

examples.en: The prop table had a labelled spot for each object we needed.
examples.zh: 「道具摆放台」上每件要用的东西都有标好的位置。

collocations: return something to the prop table

words.enDefinition: the person responsible for sourcing and managing props for a production

examples.en: Our prop master found an old phone for the opening scene.
examples.zh: 我们的「道具主管」为开场戏找来了一部旧电话。

examples.en: The prop master checked that the suitcase was back before the second act.
examples.zh: 「道具主管」在第二幕开始前确认行李箱已经归位。

words.enDefinition: the person who designs the physical scenery for a production

examples.en: The set designer drew a flat with very little furniture for our play.
examples.zh: 「舞台布景设计师」为我们的剧画了一套没几件家具的公寓。

examples.en: Our set designer gave the library scene a wall of painted books.
examples.zh: 我们的「舞台布景设计师」为图书馆那场戏画了一墙的书。

words.enDefinition: a painted or printed background used behind performers on stage

examples.en: Our scenic backdrop showed the university town in summer from across the river.
examples.zh: 我们的「舞台背景幕」上画的是从河对岸看去的夏日大学城。

examples.en: I helped paint the trees on the scenic backdrop after afternoon class.
examples.zh: 下午下课后，我帮忙在「舞台背景幕」上画树。

words.enDefinition: a transition when the performance moves to a new stage setting

examples.en: The piano played during the scene change while the actors moved offstage.
examples.zh: 演员离开舞台时，钢琴在「换景」期间演奏。

examples.en: The scene change only took a moment because we moved one table.
examples.zh: 我们只挪了一张桌子，所以很快就完成了「换景」。

words.enDefinition: to take down and remove scenery after a production

examples.en: We stayed to strike the set after the last performance on Saturday night.
examples.zh: 周六晚最后一场演出结束后，我们留下来「拆除舞台布景」。

examples.en: The company planned to strike the set before the next group moved in.
examples.zh: 剧团计划在下一组人进来之前「拆除舞台布景」。

words.enDefinition: someone who controls a spotlight that follows performers onstage

examples.en: The spotlight operator met with us before we went through the ending.
examples.zh: 我们走排结尾段之前，「追光灯操作员」先和我们碰了个面。

examples.en: My roommate volunteered as a spotlight operator for the drama club this term.
examples.zh: 室友这学期自愿担任戏剧社的「追光灯操作员」。

words.enDefinition: a control desk used to operate the lights for a production

examples.en: Our technician sat at the lighting board and waited for the signal.
examples.zh: 我们的技术人员坐在「灯光控制台」前，等待信号。

examples.en: I watched the rehearsal from a chair beside the lighting board.
examples.zh: 我坐在「灯光控制台」旁边的椅子上观看排练。

words.enDefinition: a planned instant or brief period of darkness during a production

examples.en: The stage blackout separated the scene in the flat from the street scene.
examples.zh: 「舞台灯光全熄」把公寓里的戏和街头那场戏隔开了。

examples.en: The audience fell quiet as soon as the stage blackout began.
examples.zh: 「舞台灯光全熄」一开始，观众就安静了下来。

words.enDefinition: to gradually darken the stage until no light can be seen

examples.en: The lights were meant to fade to black during the last note.
examples.zh: 本来灯光该在最后一个音符响起时「渐暗至全黑」。

examples.en: I watched the stage fade to black before the performers came out again.
examples.zh: 我看着舞台「渐暗至全黑」，随后表演者再次上场。

collocations: wait for the lights to fade to black
fade to black at the end

words.enDefinition: a technique where a performer speaks directly to the audience

examples.en: The actor used direct address to ask us what we would do.
examples.zh: 演员「直接向观众讲话」，问我们会怎么做。

examples.en: Our tutor explained how direct address changed the mood of the sketch.
examples.zh: 老师解释了「直接向观众讲话」如何改变这个短剧的气氛。

words.enDefinition: to acknowledge the audience or acknowledge that the story is fictional

examples.en: The student director wanted to break the fourth wall without changing the original ending.
examples.zh: 学生导演想在保留原结局的情况下「打破第四面墙」。

examples.en: We decided to break the fourth wall by having a character notice the applause.
examples.zh: 我们让一个角色意识到台下有人鼓掌，以此「打破第四面墙」。

collocations: choose to break the fourth wall
use a joke to break the fourth wall
actors who break the fourth wall

words.enDefinition: to keep behaving like the character you are portraying

examples.en: It was hard to stay in character when someone dropped the prop phone.
examples.zh: 有人把道具电话掉在地上时，很难「保持角色状态」。

examples.en: My partner managed to stay in character even though half the cast laughed.
examples.zh: 虽然半数演员都笑了，搭档还是「保持了角色状态」。

collocations: stay in character throughout a scene

words.enDefinition: the way a character's personality or motivations are revealed over time

examples.en: I thought the character development was strongest in the quieter second act.
examples.zh: 我觉得比较安静的第二幕「角色塑造」做得最好。

examples.en: We talked about character development after watching two versions of the same play.
examples.zh: 看完同一部剧的两个版本后，我们讨论了「角色塑造」。

words.zhGloss: 故意让观众听见的耳语
words.enDefinition: a loud whisper intended to be heard by the audience
acceptedZhAnswers: 故意让观众听见的耳语

examples.en: The actor used a stage whisper so we could hear the secret.
examples.zh: 演员用「故意让观众听见的耳语」把秘密说了出来。

examples.en: Her stage whisper was the only sound in the theatre for a moment.
examples.zh: 一时间，剧场里唯一的声音就是她「故意让观众听见的耳语」。

words.enDefinition: to speak clearly and strongly enough to be heard far away

examples.en: You need to project your voice so the back row can hear your name.
examples.zh: 你得「让声音传到观众席」，这样最后一排才能听清你的名字。

examples.en: It takes practice to project your voice without sounding like you are shouting.
examples.zh: 要做到「让声音传到观众席」，又不让人觉得在喊，需要练习。

collocations: practise how to project your voice
project your voice to the back row

words.enDefinition: a complete song or dance section within a stage musical

examples.en: Our favourite musical number used chairs to create different shapes onstage.
examples.zh: 我们最喜欢的「音乐剧歌舞段落」用椅子在舞台上摆出了不同的形状。

examples.en: The class rehearsed one musical number before working on the dialogue again.
examples.zh: 全班排练完一个「音乐剧歌舞段落」，再接着磨台词。

words.enDefinition: a song originally written for a stage musical

examples.en: My classmate sang a show tune at the end of our workshop.
examples.zh: 工作坊最后，同学唱了一首「音乐剧歌曲」。

examples.en: I recognised the show tune from a recording of last year's musical.
examples.zh: 我听过去年的音乐剧录音，认出了这首「音乐剧歌曲」。

words.enDefinition: music performed in person alongside a singer, dancer, or actor

examples.en: The dancers worked with live accompaniment at their last two rehearsals.
examples.zh: 舞者最后两次排练有「现场伴奏」配合。

examples.en: The song felt different with live accompaniment from two student musicians.
examples.zh: 有两位学生乐手「现场伴奏」，这首歌听起来不太一样。

words.enDefinition: a planned performance where dancers show prepared pieces to an audience

examples.en: My housemate performed in the dance recital near the end of term.
examples.zh: 临近期末，室友参加了「舞蹈汇报演出」。

examples.en: We met our classmates after the dance recital at the small theatre.
examples.zh: 小剧场的「舞蹈汇报演出」结束后，我们见到了同学。

words.enDefinition: a style of dance that explores varied, expressive movement

examples.en: I watched a contemporary dance performance arranged by the university's arts department.
examples.zh: 我看了学校艺术系安排的一场「当代舞」演出。

examples.en: The class used contemporary dance to explore movement in small spaces.
examples.zh: 课上，同学们用「当代舞」探索如何在小空间里活动身体。

words.enDefinition: a dance style using shoes that produce rhythmic tapping sounds

examples.en: Their tap dance could be heard clearly from the other room.
examples.zh: 在隔壁房间也能听清他们跳「踢踏舞」的声音。

examples.en: My classmate tried tap dance for the first time at an arts workshop.
examples.zh: 同学在一次艺术工作坊里第一次尝试了「踢踏舞」。

words.enDefinition: a dance for two performers in a ballet

examples.en: The pas de deux was the only piece performed by exactly two dancers.
examples.zh: 「芭蕾双人舞」是唯一只由两位舞者表演的节目。

examples.en: We watched a pas de deux during the second part of the ballet recital.
examples.zh: 芭蕾汇报演出的后半场，我们看了一段「芭蕾双人舞」。

words.enDefinition: stiff ballet shoes designed to support dancing on the toes

examples.en: She left her pointe shoes beside the other dancers' bags backstage.
examples.zh: 她把「芭蕾足尖鞋」放在后台其他舞者的包旁边。

examples.en: The costume display included an old pair of pointe shoes from the school.
examples.zh: 服装展里有一双学校收藏的旧「芭蕾足尖鞋」。

words.enDefinition: the group of ballet dancers performing together in an ensemble

examples.en: The corps de ballet returned to the stage after the two principal dancers.
examples.zh: 两位首席舞者之后，「芭蕾群舞团」重新回到舞台上。

examples.en: I could see the whole corps de ballet form a line across the stage.
examples.zh: 我看到整个「芭蕾群舞团」在台上排成一横排。

collocations: dance in the corps de ballet

words.enDefinition: a short sequence of related movements forming a complete unit

examples.en: We learned the same dance phrase and performed it in different directions.
examples.zh: 我们学了同一个「舞蹈动作组合」，再朝不同方向表演。

examples.en: She used one short dance phrase near the beginning of her piece.
examples.zh: 她在作品开头附近用了一个简短的「舞蹈动作组合」。

words.enDefinition: to practise dance movements lightly without performing them at full intensity

examples.en: We decided to mark the choreography while waiting for the pianist to arrive.
examples.zh: 我们决定边等钢琴手过来，边「简化走一遍舞蹈动作」。

examples.en: The instructor asked us to mark the choreography so she could check our timing.
examples.zh: 老师请我们「简化走一遍舞蹈动作」，她好检查节奏是否对得上。

collocations: ask dancers to mark the choreography

words.enDefinition: an arrangement of dancers in relation to one another onstage

examples.en: The dance formation changed as soon as the second piece of music began.
examples.zh: 第二段音乐一响起来，「舞蹈队形」就变了。

examples.en: We practised the dance formation in a bigger room that afternoon.
examples.zh: 那天下午，我们在更大的房间里练了「舞蹈队形」。

words.enDefinition: a dance performance made for two people to perform together

examples.en: I watched a dance duet that two students had choreographed together.
examples.zh: 我看了一段「双人舞」，是两位同学一起编的。

examples.en: Their dance duet used slow turns and long pauses without any music.
examples.zh: 他们的「双人舞」用了缓慢的转身和很长的停顿，没有配乐。

words.enDefinition: a form of live comedy usually performed by one person speaking

examples.en: The college hosted a night of stand-up comedy by students and local performers.
examples.zh: 学院办了一场「单口喜剧」之夜，由学生和本地表演者上台。

examples.en: I tried stand-up comedy because I wanted to make my classmates laugh.
examples.zh: 我尝试表演「单口喜剧」，因为想逗同学笑。

words.enDefinition: a prepared series of jokes or routines performed as one piece

examples.en: My roommate practised a five-minute comedy set before the student show.
examples.zh: 学生公演前，室友练了一段五分钟的「喜剧表演」。

examples.en: We heard a comedy set about getting lost on a huge campus.
examples.zh: 我们听了一段在大校园里迷路的「喜剧表演」。

words.enDefinition: a group that performs scenes they make up on the spot

examples.en: I went to see the improv troupe perform in the student centre.
examples.zh: 我去学生中心看了「即兴表演团」的演出。

examples.en: The improv troupe used a suggestion about laundry for its first scene.
examples.zh: 「即兴表演团」用一个关于洗衣的点子演了第一场戏。

words.enDefinition: improvised performance made up of short separate scenes or games

examples.en: The group began with short-form improv before trying a longer story together.
examples.zh: 这组人先做了「短形式即兴表演」，再合演一个更长的故事。

examples.en: We tried short-form improv at a workshop run by two older students.
examples.zh: 两位高年级同学办的工作坊上，我们尝试了「短形式即兴表演」。

words.enDefinition: using pace and pauses to make a performance funnier

examples.en: Her comedic timing made a simple story about the bus surprisingly funny.
examples.zh: 她的「喜剧节奏把握」得很好，把一个简单的公交故事讲得意外好笑。

examples.en: Our tutor explained how comedic timing could change the effect of the last line.
examples.zh: 老师讲了「喜剧节奏把握」如何改变最后一句台词的效果。

words.enDefinition: the opening part of a joke that prepares listeners for its ending

examples.en: My partner shortened the joke setup so we reached the ending sooner.
examples.zh: 搭档缩短了「笑话铺垫」，这样我们更快就能讲到结尾。

examples.en: The joke setup mentioned a lost umbrella before the story took a turn.
examples.zh: 「笑话铺垫」提到一把丢了的伞，之后故事来了个转折。

words.enDefinition: the final line or part of a joke that provokes laughter

examples.en: The performer waited a beat before delivering the punchline of the joke.
examples.zh: 表演者停了一拍，才抖出这段笑话的「包袱」。

examples.en: I guessed the punchline before my friend finished telling the joke.
examples.zh: 朋友还没讲完笑话，我就猜到了「包袱」在哪里。

words.enDefinition: a joke short enough to be told in a single sentence

examples.en: The comedian opened with a one-liner about the campus coffee queue.
examples.zh: 喜剧演员拿校园咖啡店的队伍讲了个「一句话笑话」开场。

examples.en: I missed the one-liner because the audience was still laughing loudly.
examples.zh: 观众还在大声笑，我没听见那个「一句话笑话」。

words.enDefinition: an idea offered by spectators as a starting point for performance

examples.en: The performers turned an audience suggestion into a scene about train travel.
examples.zh: 表演者把一个「观众给的点子」演成了一场关于火车旅行的戏。

examples.en: My classmate offered an audience suggestion, and the group used it immediately.
examples.zh: 同学给了一个「观众点子」，表演团马上用了。

words.enDefinition: the part of a live act involving interaction with audience members

examples.en: She did a little crowd work after a visitor laughed at the wrong moment.
examples.zh: 有位观众笑得不是时候，她就「现场与观众即兴互动」了几句。

examples.en: The comedian used crowd work to learn where people were studying.
examples.zh: 喜剧演员借着「现场与观众即兴互动」了解大家都在哪儿上学。

collocations: crowd work with the front row

words.enDefinition: an audience member who interrupts a performer by calling out

examples.en: A heckler kept interrupting until one of the ushers spoke to him.
examples.zh: 一个「起哄打断演出的人」一直在插嘴，直到有位引座员找他谈了话。

examples.en: The comedian paused after a heckler shouted from the back row.
examples.zh: 一个「起哄打断演出的人」从最后一排喊了一声，喜剧演员停了下来。

words.enDefinition: theatre that tells a story chiefly through movement and physical expression

examples.en: The physical theatre piece told its story almost entirely through movement.
examples.zh: 这部「肢体剧场」作品几乎完全用动作讲故事。

examples.en: Our tutor invited a physical theatre company to perform in the studio.
examples.zh: 老师邀请了一家「肢体剧场」剧团到工作室演出。

words.enDefinition: a live performance of poetry or expressive writing spoken aloud

examples.en: I attended a spoken-word performance where students shared poetry about their hometowns.
examples.zh: 我参加了一场「口语诗表演」，同学们朗诵了写家乡的诗。

examples.en: Her spoken-word performance used pauses to make the words stand out.
examples.zh: 她在「口语诗表演」中用停顿来突出一些词。

words.enDefinition: a booklet giving information about a production and its performers

examples.en: I checked the theatre programme to see who played the main character.
examples.zh: 我翻了翻「剧场节目册」，看看谁演主角。

examples.en: The theatre programme included two pages about how the students developed the piece.
examples.zh: 「剧场节目册」里有两页介绍同学们是如何创作这部作品的。

words.enDefinition: a public show presented before a production officially opens

examples.en: I saw the preview performance before the cast changed part of the ending.
examples.zh: 结尾有一段改动之前，我看了「正式首演前的试演场」。

examples.en: The theatre invited students to the preview performance on a weekday afternoon.
examples.zh: 剧场邀请同学们在一个工作日的下午观看「正式首演前的试演场」。

words.enDefinition: the first official evening performance of a stage production

examples.en: My flatmate brought flowers for the cast on opening night last month.
examples.zh: 上个月的「首演之夜」，室友给演出人员带了花。

examples.en: I couldn't sleep the night before opening night because I was nervous.
examples.zh: 「首演之夜」前一晚，我紧张得睡不着。

words.enDefinition: the final public performance in a series of shows

examples.en: I booked for the closing performance because my sister was visiting then.
examples.zh: 我订了「收官演出」的票，因为妹妹那时会来。

examples.en: The director thanked the student volunteers after the closing performance that evening.
examples.zh: 当晚「收官演出」结束后，导演向学生志愿者致谢。

collocations: final bow at the closing performance

words.enDefinition: a break between parts of a performance, often between acts

examples.en: We talked about the first act outside the theatre during intermission.
examples.zh: 「中场休息」时，我们在剧场外聊了聊第一幕。

examples.en: The pianist came back to play another piece after the intermission.
examples.zh: 「中场休息」结束后，钢琴手回来又弹了一首曲子。

words.enDefinition: lights that illuminate the audience area in a theatre

examples.en: We put our programmes away as the house lights began to dim.
examples.zh: 「观众席照明」开始变暗时，我们把节目册收了起来。

examples.en: The house lights came up while the performers were still applauding the crew.
examples.zh: 表演者还在为工作人员鼓掌时，「观众席照明」亮了起来。

collocations: wait for the house lights to come on

words.enDefinition: the moment after a performance when the cast acknowledges applause

examples.en: The dancers returned to the stage for a curtain call at the end.
examples.zh: 演出结束时，舞者回到台上「谢幕」。

examples.en: The entire cast wore their final costumes during the curtain call that night.
examples.zh: 那晚「演员谢幕」时，整个剧组都还穿着最后一场的戏服。

collocations: come out for a curtain call

words.enDefinition: to bend forward briefly to acknowledge applause after a performance

examples.en: The violinist returned to take a bow beside the two student actors.
examples.zh: 小提琴手回到台上，站在两位学生演员旁「鞠躬致意」。

examples.en: Our director told us to take a bow together at the very end.
examples.zh: 导演让我们在最后一起「鞠躬致意」。

collocations: come out to take a bow
take a bow with the cast
take a bow at the end

words.enDefinition: enthusiastic applause from audience members standing rather than sitting

examples.en: The student cast received a standing ovation after the closing performance.
examples.zh: 收官演出结束后，观众向学生演员们「起立鼓掌致敬」。

examples.en: I joined the standing ovation because my roommate had danced so well.
examples.zh: 室友跳得太好了，我也跟着大家一起「起立鼓掌致敬」。

words.enDefinition: a discussion where audiences and performers talk after a show

examples.en: We stayed for the post-show talkback to ask about the painted scenery.
examples.zh: 我们留下参加「演后交流」，询问彩绘布景的事。

examples.en: The playwright joined our post-show talkback from another city by video.
examples.zh: 剧作家从另一个城市通过视频参加了我们的「演后交流」。

words.enDefinition: a show that displays spoken words and relevant sounds as text

examples.en: We chose the captioned performance so we could read the dialogue as well.
examples.zh: 我们选了「带字幕的演出」，这样也能读到台词。

examples.en: The theatre marked the captioned performance with a small symbol in the programme.
examples.zh: 剧场在节目册里用一个小符号标出了「带字幕的演出」。

words.enDefinition: a show with spoken descriptions of its important visual details

examples.en: My classmate asked if the student ballet had an audio-described performance.
examples.zh: 同学向剧场询问学生芭蕾有没有「带口述影像的演出」。

examples.en: The audio-described performance included descriptions of the dancers' movements between sections of music.
examples.zh: 那场「带口述影像的演出」在各段音乐之间有对舞者动作的口述说明。

words.enDefinition: a show adapted to welcome people with different sensory needs

examples.en: At our relaxed performance, the house lights stayed partly on throughout the show.
examples.zh: 我们去的「感官友好场次」，观众席灯光在整场演出中没有完全熄灭。

examples.en: The programme explained how the relaxed performance would differ from the evening show.
examples.zh: 节目册介绍了「感官友好场次」与晚场会有哪些不同。

words.enDefinition: a chance for audience members to explore props or scenery by touch

examples.en: A volunteer introduced the props during a touch tour before the performance.
examples.zh: 一名志愿者在「演前触摸导览」上介绍了道具。

examples.en: The touch tour included some fabric samples from the show's costumes.
examples.zh: 「演前触摸导览」包含了演出服装的几块面料样品。

words.enDefinition: a show where an interpreter renders the dialogue in sign language

examples.en: The interpreter stood beside the stage throughout the sign-interpreted performance that evening.
examples.zh: 当晚「有手语传译的演出」期间，译员全程站在舞台旁。

examples.en: We checked which evening shows had a sign-interpreted performance listed online.
examples.zh: 我们在网上查找晚间场次中哪些是「有手语传译的演出」。

words.enDefinition: translated words displayed above a stage during an opera or play

examples.en: I followed the surtitles when I couldn't understand the Italian words.
examples.zh: 听不懂意大利语唱词时，我就跟着看「舞台上方的译文字幕」。

examples.en: The opera used surtitles that we could read from the back row.
examples.zh: 这场歌剧使用了「舞台上方的译文字幕」，坐在最后一排也能看清。

words.enDefinition: parts of a performance where spectators are invited to take part

examples.en: The play used audience participation in a scene where students voted together.
examples.zh: 这部剧在同学们一起投票的那场戏中安排了「观众参与」。

examples.en: The programme explained that audience participation would be optional throughout the show.
examples.zh: 节目册说明，全场「观众参与」环节都可以自愿选择。

words.enDefinition: a notice asking people not to take photos during a show

examples.en: The programme said "No photography during the performance," so I kept my phone in my bag.
examples.zh: 节目册写着「演出进行时请勿拍照」，所以我没把手机从包里拿出来。

examples.en: An announcement repeated "No photography during the performance," just before the house lights went down.
examples.zh: 观众席照明暗下来前，广播又提醒了一遍「演出进行时请勿拍照」。

collocations: notice saying no photography during the performance
sign reading no photography during the performance
reminder of no photography during the performance

words.enDefinition: the art of using puppets to tell stories onstage

examples.en: Our drama group explored puppetry using figures made from folded paper.
examples.zh: 戏剧小组用纸折的人偶探索「木偶表演艺术」。

examples.en: I was surprised by how expressive puppetry could be without dialogue.
examples.zh: 没想到即使没有台词，「木偶表演艺术」也能这么有表现力。

words.enDefinition: makeup used to shape a performer's appearance for an audience

examples.en: The actors could see their stage makeup clearly under the rehearsal lights.
examples.zh: 演员在排练灯光下能清楚看见自己的「舞台妆」。

examples.en: I removed my stage makeup before getting the bus back to campus.
examples.zh: 我先卸掉「舞台妆」，然后坐公交回学校。

words.enDefinition: someone who designs the clothing worn in a production

examples.en: The costume designer brought three different sketches to our first rehearsal.
examples.zh: 「戏服设计师」带着三张不同的草图来参加第一次排练。

examples.en: Our costume designer asked how easily I could move in the coat.
examples.zh: 我们的「戏服设计师」问我穿上那件外套活动起来是否方便。

words.enDefinition: a performer who keeps the choreography consistent throughout a production

examples.en: The dance captain helped the new dancers learn the existing number.
examples.zh: 「舞蹈排练领队」帮新来的舞者熟悉已经编好的歌舞段落。

examples.en: Our dance captain made notes after watching us rehearse the final section.
examples.zh: 看完我们排练最后一段后，「舞蹈排练领队」记下了要点。

collocations: rehearsal led by a dance captain

words.enDefinition: a self-contained solo song within an opera, usually with accompaniment

examples.en: We practised a short aria in class with a student pianist.
examples.zh: 我们在课上练了一段简短的「歌剧咏叹调」，有同学弹钢琴伴奏。

examples.en: The audience went unusually quiet during the singer's final aria.
examples.zh: 歌手唱最后一段「歌剧咏叹调」时，观众格外安静。

words.enDefinition: the written text of an opera, including sung and spoken words

examples.en: I read the libretto before the opera so I knew the story.
examples.zh: 看歌剧前，我读了「歌剧唱词剧本」，好先了解剧情。

examples.en: The tutor gave us a translation of the libretto in class.
examples.zh: 老师在课上发给我们一份「歌剧唱词剧本」译本。
